title: Karnataka High Court Appoints Arbitrator in Rs. 2.53 Crore Air Force College Construction Dispute
case_name: Varsha Constructions v. Military Engineer Services & Ors.
citation: CMP No. 150 of 2026 (Karnataka High Court, Justice H.T. Narendra Prasad)
card_summary: The Karnataka High Court appointed a retired District Judge as sole arbitrator on a contractor's Section 11(6) petition against the Military Engineer Services, over an Air Force Technical College building contract. The final bill claimed Rs. 2.53 crore for extra works and escalation, and three notices sent over 2024 and 2025 went unanswered. The respondents stayed unrepresented, and all claims were left open.
card_tip: A government counterparty's silence on arbitration notices does not stall a claim; file a Section 11(6) petition with proof of service of each notice to get an arbitrator appointed on default.
verification_notes: Confirmed from the LiveLawBiz news report and the order text it uploaded, which match on the bench, the appointee, the Rs. 2,53,33,586 claim figure, the three notice dates, and the October 8, 2026 order date.
